model: Envision Single Compressor Water-to-Water Heat Pump (FX10)
applies_to: WaterFurnace Envision single-compressor water-to-water heat pumps with the FX10 DDC controller.
summary: BACnet objects for WaterFurnace's single-compressor Envision water-to-water heat pump on the FX10 controller. The BAS sends the compressor (Y1) and reversing valve calls and can shut the unit down or reset lockouts. Statuses (compressor, valve, accessory outputs, flow switches, alarm) are multistate inputs, and AI14 gives an alarm code.
notes: Output-type points are volatile and fall back to uncommanded after a power cycle; unlimited writes.
No engineering units are printed in the source; temperatures are presumably degrees F.
Instance numbers have gaps as printed: AI jumps from 8 to 14 and MO4 is not listed.
MI4 LoadPmpStatus and MI5 SrcPmpStatus are described as the accessory 1 and 2 outputs.
MO2 Valve Enable is listed as 1=Cooling, 2=Heating but MI3 Rev Vlv Status as 1=Heating, 2=Cooling; confirm on site.
The sheet does not state the BACnet transport.

integration.summary: The BAS stages this unit directly with MO1 (compressor Y1 call) and MO2 (reversing valve). MO3 gives a network emergency shutdown and MO5 resets lockouts. Supervise it with the load water temperatures, MI1 mode and the AI14 alarm code.
integration.enable: There is no internal temperature control or enable point: the unit runs only on external compressor (Y1) and reversing valve (O) calls, sent either at the terminal board or over the network. Emergency shutdown comes from MO3 Emerg Override (5=Shutdown) or a closed contact on BI-2.
setup: Freeze limits are 30 F with the BI-4/BI-5 jumpers installed and 15 F with them removed.
gotchas: Output points (AO/MO) are volatile and go back to uncommanded after a power cycle, so rewrite them after power is restored.
A Y1 call turns on X1 first; the compressor starts after a fixed 90-second delay and then runs at least 2 minutes.
Three faults during one heating or cooling call put the unit in lockout until reset by power cycle or MO5.
After power-up or leaving emergency shutdown, outputs wait a random 1-120 second start delay.
MO2 and MI3 list opposite state orders for heating and cooling; verify the valve direction on site.
